title: A Classical Sequential Growth Dynamics for Causal Sets
version: arXiv:gr-qc/9904062v3, 26 June 2004; Phys. Rev. D 61, 024002 (2000). Read whole through a text extraction; figures not seen.
locator: Sec. 1.1 (labels as gauge; 'no meaningful order of birth'); Sec. 2 (transitive percolation, posts); Sec. 3 (internal temporality, discrete general covariance, Bell causality); Sec. 4 (originary percolation; eqs. 6, 7, 12; P(C)=W p^L q^(C(n,2)-R)); Sec. 4.5 (sample cosmologies); Sec. 5 (eqs. 17-18; stem conjecture)
assumptions: Classical Markov growth; internal temporality; discrete general covariance; Bell causality; no vanishing transition probability (generic case).
conclusion: Authors' result: the generic solutions are parametrised by t_n >= 0, with transition probability lambda(w,m)/lambda(n,0). Authors' claim: birth order beyond the causal order is gauge. The paper does not discuss order reversal.
proof_status: Derivation given in the paper; not independently re-derived here. Formula implemented and checked for normalisation and label independence to n=7.
dependencies: Rideout thesis (ref. 19) for some proofs: not read.
relevance: Defines the dynamics tested. Source for the gauge status of birth order.
limits: Figures not seen in the extraction.

title: Evidence for a continuum limit in causal set dynamics
version: arXiv:gr-qc/0003117, read through the ar5iv HTML rendering; arXiv version number not recorded by that rendering.
locator: Introduction ('an underlying time-reversal invariance'); Sec. 6 discussion of figures 10-11 ('due to the time-reversal symmetry of the percolation dynamics', equality of abundances of an order and its reverse)
conclusion: Authors state and use the time-reversal symmetry of percolation.
proof_status: Stated, not proved there; follows from the static description. Confirmed exactly here for n<=7.
relevance: Prior statement of the percolation half of the verdict.
limits: Only the passages matching 'time-reversal' were read.

title: 'Observables' in causal set cosmology
version: arXiv:gr-qc/0210061v2, 20 October 2002; whole text read through an extraction.
locator: Sec. 2 (past-finite sample space, covariant sigma-algebra, posts); Sec. 3 Theorem 1, Propositions 1-2, Corollary 1; Sec. 4 Lemma 4; Sec. 7
assumptions: Generic CSG family with t_k>0 for some k>=2; all relabellings are gauge.
conclusion: Authors' theorem: stem sets generate the covariant measurable sets up to measure zero.
proof_status: Proved in the paper; proof read, not re-derived.
dependencies: Mackey's theorem on Borel spaces: not read.
relevance: Physical questions are stem questions, which are one-sided; labels are gauge.

title: Relativity theory does not imply that the future already exists: a counterexample
locator: Secs. 2, 5 (birth order 'an artifact of the description', 'pure gauge'; stopping at a stage has no objective meaning), 6 (Minkowski regions only with vanishingly small probability), 7
assumptions: CSG models as a model of becoming.
conclusion: Author's claim: CSG models show becoming is compatible with relativity; the birth order beyond the causal order is gauge.
relevance: Authors' view of what is physical in growth.

title: What becomes of a causal set
version: arXiv:1502.00018v1, 30 January 2015; abstract, the Sec. 4 passages on label gauge (Alice and Bob example) and the closing paragraph of Sec. 4 read through an extraction.
locator: Abstract; Sec. 4 (labels as gauge; gauge-invariant growth in cardinality); end of Sec. 4: 'despite appearances transitive percolation is perfectly time reversal invariant', growth to future and past
conclusion: Authors' claims: labelled growth conflicts with the gauge reading; percolation is time-reversal invariant; two-way and past-infinite growth are possible.
relevance: Prior statement of the percolation half; source of the two-way growth idea.
limits: Not read whole. Their Sec. 3 on Stein's theorem is treated in the project's becoming_causets.tex, not here.

title: If time had no beginning: growth dynamics for past-infinite causal sets
version: arXiv:2109.10749, read through the ar5iv HTML rendering (version number not recorded); Class. Quantum Grav. 39 (2022) 045002 per search result, not checked.
locator: Sec. 1 ('must have a beginning, by definition of the model'); Sec. 3.2: Lemma 3.4, Claim 3.5 and its proof, causal immortality and Claim 3.6 (start); Sec. 4 opening (stage order is gauge); Sec. 5
assumptions: Alternating growth: births alternately to the future and to the past, same couplings.
conclusion: Authors' results: percolation and alternating percolation agree at every finite stage, and only for percolation (Lemma 3.4, proof cited to their refs. 21-22); only alternating percolation is label-covariant (Claim 3.5, proved in the text).
proof_status: Claim 3.5 proof read. Lemma 3.4 proof not in this paper.
dependencies: Refs. 21, 22 (not identified or read); Alon-Bollobas-Brightwell-Janson 1994 (not read).
relevance: Closest prior art for Proposition A; states that the beginning is definitional.
limits: Sec. 2.3, most of Sec. 4 and the appendices not read.

title: A manifestly covariant framework for causal set dynamics
version: arXiv:1910.07292, ar5iv HTML rendering; abstract and passages on gauge read (Secs. 1, 2.3, 3 opening, 5 opening).
conclusion: Authors' claims: the sequence of births is a total order containing unphysical gauge information; covtree gives a label-free random walk whose observables are stem events.
relevance: The brief's 'Dowker-Zalel on covariant growth'. Confirms the gauge reading; covtree is built from stems and is one-sided.
limits: Body and proofs not read. Zalel's follow-up on the structure of covtree seen only in a search result (discovery).
